articleTitle: IEE Colloquium on 'Enhanced and Widescreen PAL' (Digest No.006)
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Enhanced and Widescreen PAL
IEE Colloquium on Enhanced and Widescreen PAL
abstract: After two years of cooperation the PALplus project has decided on the PALplus system architecture. In these two years, aspects of format conversion, improved Y/C separation, backwards compatible transmission, sound improvements, and echo cancellation techniques have been studied in various European laboratories. Two series of subjective tests have been carried out in order to find the best performing algorithm from the various proposals. The paper outlines the architecture of the system and introduces the techniques used in the various stages of the video signal processing.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Enhanced and Widescreen PAL
abstract: Two types of transmission path are present from the TV studios for the PALplus picture enhancement signal: the studio to transmitter link, the transmitter, radio path to the receiver; and the contribution circuits to and from other companies or network centres. The telecommunication circuits used for the studio to transmitter link vary considerably from baseband cable, RF carrier on cable, microwave FM, fibre optic FM, fibre optic digital circuits, or any combination.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Enhanced and Widescreen PAL
abstract: The BBC, as befits a broadcaster, was concerned with improved coding for use within and between studio centres with minimal impact on the requirements of domestic viewing equipment. In particular, a great deal of work was carried out on the separation of luminance and chrominance using two and three dimensional filtering and motion adaptive methods. The paper describes the history of investigations into improved PAL coding by the BBC, leading up to the advent of PALplus.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Enhanced and Widescreen PAL
abstract: The most significant European activity for enhanced compatible PAL is concentrated within the PALplus consortium. The consortium comprises the major European receiver and broadcast manufacturers, broadcasters from Germany, Austria and Switzerland, and the UK is represented by the BBC and UK Independent Broadcasting. PALplus activities are separated into a number of working groups, one of which is studying implications for the production studio. The work broadly covers three areas, the studio standard, the production studio, and the studio centre including internal and external communications. The article outlines some of the considerations of wide-screen 16:9 production under these three headings.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Enhanced and Widescreen PAL
abstract: The project PAL-plus was constituted in 1989 and it consists of broadcasters from Germany, Switzerland, Austria and the UK as well as the major European consumer electronics industry, namely the Grundig-group, Nokia, Philips and Thomson. The basic idea to work together on the enhancement of the PAL-system could be explained in the best manner by describing the European situation regarding the transmission of TV-signals.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Letterbox in the UK? (PAL TV system)
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Enhanced and Widescreen PAL
abstract: There are three basic approaches to the transmission of a 16:9 aspect ratio image using the PAL system: the 'letterbox' method, the 'side-panel' method, and a compromise letterbox approach sometimes referred to as a 'window' method. Each has particular advantages and disadvantages. It will be shown that the UK terrestrial broadcasters consider that there would be advantages in being able to choose to transmit some programmes, for a temporary period only, in a compromise letterbox format, as a means of easing the introduction of PALplus, which uses a 16:9 letterbox.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Enhanced and Widescreen PAL
abstract: Discusses the evaluations made within the framework of the PALplus group to assess both the PALplus quality and the compatible quality of several candidate algorithms, based on simulations. Since the detailed information is confidential to the members of the PALplus group, the paper focuses on the methodology and on the implementation.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Enhanced and Widescreen PAL
abstract: Echoes can occur in any communication system where more than one signal path is available between the transmitter and the receiver. In television such echoes are usually called ghosts, because the effect on the received picture is to produce faint repeat images of the main picture. In the light of plans for European broadcasters to introduce wide screen television services based on enhancements to the existing PAL system, consideration should be given to the effect of echoes on such enhanced systems and techniques which can be used to reduce these effects.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Enhanced and Widescreen PAL
abstract: As far as the PAL countries are concerned, the FM sound carrier power was often reduced relative to vision power as the sound circuitry of the receiver increased in sophistication. The attainable picture quality could then improve, but when experimental sound enhancements, such as subcarrier stereo were introduced, the quality of the sound was not as good as expected. In addition, pictures as well as sound could deteriorate in older receivers. A major problem of any sound enhancement continues to be the backward compatibility with existing receivers.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>
